item.title: Why Is a 100-Year-Old Vaccine Still Our Only Defense Against the World’s Deadliest Infectious Disease?
item.description: Tuberculosis (TB), the world’s oldest infectious disease, is also one of its deadliest. In 2024 alone, TB killed about 1.23 million people — more than the combined tolls from malaria and HIV/AIDS combined. But unlike the urgent flashes of panic that accompany other global health crises, such as COVID-19 and Ebola, TB rarely dominates headlines anymore, nor does it trigger emergency responses from policymakers. item.title: 2025 Recap: How Global Citizens Drove Measurable Progress in a Defining Year
item.description: This year marked an important milestone for Global Citizen’s movement. item.title: Two Drops and a Long Walk: Inside Mozambique’s Door-to-Door Polio Vaccination Drive
item.description: Polio vaccination workers don't just deliver two lifesaving drops — sometimes they even name a child. item.title: How Improved Finance Access Is Shaping a New Approach to Sustainable Production in the Amazon
item.description: Cametá, located in the state of Pará along the banks of the Tocantins River, has a history spanning nearly 390 years. The city is known for hosting what is often called the “largest carnival in the Amazon”, a tradition that for more than 150 years has brought people together from across the region. item.title: How Banco do Brasil Supports Reforestation and the Bioeconomy
item.description: Across the Amazon, hundreds of communities depend on forest-based livelihoods rooted in traditional knowledge, sustainable production, and long-term stewardship of the land. item.description: As a polio vaccination team wound their way on foot towards a row of grass-roofed houses in a small village in Inhambane province, Mozambique, a voice carried on the wind. Mixed with the sounds of children playing and a rooster calling was a radio show. In the most remote corners of the country, radio still reaches listeners. item.title: Finance for All: How Sustainable Credit Can Reach Isolated Communities in the Amazon Region
item.description: Açaí, often called the “black gold of the Amazon”, is more than just a food source. For many families, it is tied to daily meals, seasonal income, and a way of life shaped by the river. Pará leads Brazil in both açaí production and exports. item.title: Young People Aren’t Just the Future — They’re the Solution. Here’s Why.
item.description: Today’s youth are made up of incredible, talented individuals who care about the world and their impact on it.
